evidence: CURRENT-DESIGN.md:9,14 permits multiple clones of one seat and specifies a serialized writer, but explicitly leaves stale-edit/precondition semantics undesigned. DESIGN-NOTES.md:149-151 makes shared seat state a separate file and queues all writes; :160 explicitly warns that serialization cannot detect a stale whole-file replacement. Concrete path: clones A and B read the same seat instructions; A submits replacement adding decision X, B independently submits replacement adding Y from the older text; absent an enforced revision/patch precondition, the worker commits A then B, and B's stale content silently removes X. This violates HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:139's explicit success criterion that two clones contribute without silently overwriting shared state. DESIGN-NOTES.md:53,58 proposes expected revisions, but CURRENT-DESIGN.md:14 and HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:149 leave the actual contract open. This is an acknowledged gap in a draft design, not an observed implementation failure; Should-fix before realizing the stated concurrency outcome.
